trigger.message: Could not start your compute. The operation was aborted due to timeout
trigger.limitation: The retained failure does not identify start POST versus operation or environment GET. It was not reproduced live.

behavior: Send the Cloud Shell start mutation exactly once.
On a transient lost start response, inspect the same default environment and require RUNNING plus the unique ephemeral SSH key before dispatch.
Retry only transient read failures, at most three attempts per read and within the provisioning deadline.
Poll the original acknowledged operation; never issue a replacement start.
Preserve authorization/quota failures, explicit operation errors, bounded deadlines and key cleanup.
Preserve response-body transport errors instead of silently treating them as empty successful data.
Persist start acceptance, uncertainty and reconciliation timestamps without provider tokens or keys.
limitations: Recovery is proven with injected unit failures; real Google timeout recovery has not yet been observed.
A provider delay can exceed the ready-compute 20-second target.
Provider shutdown, VM replacement durability and Codespaces browser acceptance are separate gates.
